settings.name: RepositoryLifecycle
settings.description: What kind of thing a repository is, declared in its owner's hub. How recently anyone committed is observed from git separately, and compared with this to name drift.

events.description: Classified as exploring an intent: its value is what it shows.
Classified as a concrete build that is not distributed.
What this prototype explored becomes a concrete implementation in the same repository. When the intent continues elsewhere, write grew-into instead and keep this state.
First distributed version: npm, PyPI, apt, a deployed service. Kept current from then on.
An archived repository comes back and is read again from the start.

states.name: Unclassified
states.prompt: Read the README, the package manifests and mw-repomap observe's git reading. Classify from evidence, not from what the README promises. Write purpose in at most 55 words, or status needs-resolution and no purpose. Every row starts revision pending.

states.name: Prototype
states.description: Explores an intent. At least a quarter of the repositories are here.
states.prompt: Name its three core features, each in at most 55 words, each with a status. Link its prototype:<slug> node when the Miadi seam holds one (public address on the node, editing address never in the row). Relate it to the repositories it grew into.

states.name: Implementation
states.description: A concrete build of an intent, not distributed.
states.prompt: Name the capabilities its features realize. Write consumes for each package or API it depends on.

states.name: Maintained
states.prompt: Keep the git reading fresh. A maintained repository with no commit in a year is drift to report, not to correct by hand.

states.name: Archived
states.description: Ended by its owner. Commits after this are drift.
states.prompt: Keep its relations: a prototype that ended is still where an intent was first seen.
